title: JEE Main 2026 · 22 Jan · Shift 2 (recreated)

qs.stem: Let the locus of the mid-point of the chord through the origin O of the parabola y<sup>2</sup> = 4x be the curve S. Let P be any point on S. Then the locus of the point, which internally divides OP in the ratio 3 : 1, is :
steps: Chord end (t<sup>2</sup>, 2t): midpoint (t<sup>2</sup>/2, t) gives k<sup>2</sup> = 2h, so S : y<sup>2</sup> = 2x.
Take P = (u<sup>2</sup>/2, u) on S. The point R dividing OP as 3 : 1 is R = (3/4)P = (3u<sup>2</sup>/8, 3u/4).
Hence 2k<sup>2</sup> = 3h, i.e. 2y<sup>2</sup> = 3x.

qs.stem:
Among the statements
(S1) : If A(5, −1) and B(−2, 3) are two vertices of a triangle, whose orthocentre is (0, 0), then its third vertex is (−4, −7)
and
(S2) : If positive numbers 2a, b, c are three consecutive terms of an A.P., then the lines ax + by + c = 0 are concurrent at (2, −2),
steps: S1: with C = (h, k), OA ⊥ BC gives 5h − k + 13 = 0 and OB ⊥ AC gives 2h − 3k − 13 = 0.
Test (−4, −7): −20 + 7 + 13 = 0 and −8 + 21 − 13 = 0, so S1 is true.
S2: 2b = 2a + c means 2a − 2b + c = 0, which says every such line passes through (2, −2). So S2 is true.

qs.stem: Let [•] denote the greatest integer function, and let f(x) = min{√2 x, x<sup>2</sup>}. Let S = {x ∈ (−2, 2) : the function g(x) = |x|[x<sup>2</sup>] is discontinuous at x}. Then ∑<sub>x∈S</sub> f(x) equals :
steps: [x<sup>2</sup>] jumps where x<sup>2</sup> = 1, 2, 3; |x| is nonzero there, so S = {±1, ±√2, ±√3}.
f(1) = 1, f(−1) = −√2; f(√2) = 2, f(−√2) = −2; f(√3) = √6, f(−√3) = −√6.
Sum = 1 − √2 + 2 − 2 + √6 − √6 = 1 − √2.

qs.stem: Let P(10, 2√15) be a point on the hyperbola x<sup>2</sup>/a<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>/b<sup>2</sup> = 1, whose foci are S and S'. If the length of its latus rectum is 8, then the square of the area of ΔPSS' is equal to :
steps: Latus rectum 2b<sup>2</sup>/a = 8 gives b<sup>2</sup> = 4a. P on curve: 100/a<sup>2</sup> − 60/(4a) = 1, so a<sup>2</sup> + 15a − 100 = 0, a = 5, b<sup>2</sup> = 20.
e<sup>2</sup> = 1 + 20/25 = 9/5, so ae = 3√5 and SS' = 6√5.
Area = (1/2)(6√5)(2√15) = 30√3, whose square is 2700.

qs.stem: Let α, β be the roots of the quadratic equation 12x<sup>2</sup> − 20x + 3λ = 0, λ ∈ Z. If 1/2 ≤ |β − α| ≤ 3/2, then the sum of all possible values of λ is :
steps: α + β = 5/3, αβ = λ/4, so (β − α)<sup>2</sup> = 25/9 − λ.
1/4 ≤ 25/9 − λ ≤ 9/4 gives 19/36 ≤ λ ≤ 91/36, i.e. 0.53 ≤ λ ≤ 2.53.
Integers: λ = 1, 2; sum = 3.

qs.stem: If X = [[x], [y], [z]] is a solution of the system of equations AX = B, where adj A = [[4, 2, 2], [−5, 0, 5], [1, −2, 3]] and B = [[4], [0], [2]], then |x + y + z| is equal to :
steps: det(adj A) = 4(10) − 2(−20) + 2(10) = 100 = |A|<sup>2</sup>, so |A| = ±10.
X = (adj A)B/|A|; (adj A)B = [20, −10, 10]<sup>T</sup>, so X = ±(2, −1, 1).
x + y + z = ±2, so |x + y + z| = 2.

qs.stem:
Let n be the number obtained on rolling a fair die. If the probability that the system
x − ny + z = 6
x + (n − 2)y + (n + 1)z = 8
(n − 1)y + z = 1
has a unique solution is k/6, then the sum of k and all possible values of n is :
steps: Determinant = −n<sup>2</sup> + 3n − 2 = −(n − 1)(n − 2), nonzero unless n = 1 or 2.
Unique solution for n = 3, 4, 5, 6: probability 4/6, so k = 4.

qs.stem: Let C<sub>r</sub> denote the coefficient of x<sup>r</sup> in the binomial expansion of (1 + x)<sup>n</sup>, n ∈ N, 0 ≤ r ≤ n. If P<sub>n</sub> = C<sub>0</sub> − C<sub>1</sub> + (2<sup>2</sup>/3)C<sub>2</sub> − (2<sup>3</sup>/4)C<sub>3</sub> + ..... + ((−2)<sup>n</sup>/(n + 1))C<sub>n</sub>, then the value of ∑<sub>n=1</sub><sup>25</sup> 1/P<sub>2n</sub> equals :
steps: P<sub>n</sub> = ∑ C<sub>r</sub>(−2)<sup>r</sup>/(r + 1) = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> (1 − 2x)<sup>n</sup> dx = [1 − (−1)<sup>n+1</sup>]/(2(n + 1)).
For even index 2n: P<sub>2n</sub> = 2/(2(2n + 1)) = 1/(2n + 1).

qs.stem: Let S and S' be the foci of the ellipse x<sup>2</sup>/25 + y<sup>2</sup>/9 = 1 and P(α, β) be a point on the ellipse in the first quadrant. If (SP)<sup>2</sup> + (S'P)<sup>2</sup> − SP · S'P = 37, then α<sup>2</sup> + β<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: SP + S'P = 10, so (SP + S'P)<sup>2</sup> − 3 SP·S'P = 37 gives SP·S'P = 21.
SP·S'P = a<sup>2</sup> − e<sup>2</sup>α<sup>2</sup> = 25 − (16/25)α<sup>2</sup> = 21, so α<sup>2</sup> = 25/4.
β<sup>2</sup> = 9(1 − 1/4) = 27/4; α<sup>2</sup> + β<sup>2</sup> = 52/4 = 13.

qs.stem: Let the domain of the function f(x) = log<sub>3</sub> log<sub>5</sub>(7 − log<sub>2</sub>(x<sup>2</sup> − 10x + 85)) + sin<sup>−1</sup>(|(3x − 7)/(17 − x)|) be (α, β]. Then α + β is equal to :
steps: log<sub>5</sub>(7 − log<sub>2</sub>(·)) > 0 needs log<sub>2</sub>(x<sup>2</sup> − 10x + 85) < 6, i.e. x<sup>2</sup> − 10x + 21 < 0, so 3 < x < 7.
On this range 17 − x > 0 and 3x − 7 > 0, so |(3x − 7)/(17 − x)| ≤ 1 means 3x − 7 ≤ 17 − x, x ≤ 6.
Domain (3, 6], so α + β = 9.

qs.stem: Let f(x) = [x]<sup>2</sup> − [x + 3] − 3, x ∈ R, where [·] is the greatest integer function. Then :
steps: f(x) = [x]<sup>2</sup> − [x] − 6 = ([x] − 3)([x] + 2).
f = 0 when [x] = 3 or −2 (whole intervals), so infinitely many zeros; f > 0 for x < −2 or x ≥ 4, so (2) is incomplete.
f < 0 iff −2 < [x] < 3, i.e. x ∈ [−1, 3): (3) holds. On [0, 2), f = −6, so the integral is −12, not −6.
opts: f(x) = 0 for finitely many values of x

qs.stem: If lim<sub>x→0</sub> [e<sup>(a−1)x</sup> + 2 cos bx + (c − 2)e<sup>−x</sup>] / [x cos x − log<sub>e</sub>(1 + x)] = 2, then a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: Denominator = x − x<sup>3</sup>/2 − (x − x<sup>2</sup>/2 + ...) = x<sup>2</sup>/2 + O(x<sup>3</sup>), so the numerator must start at x<sup>2</sup>.
Constant term: 1 + 2 + c − 2 = 0, c = −1. x term: (a − 1) − (c − 2) = 0, a = −2.
x<sup>2</sup> coefficient: (a − 1)<sup>2</sup>/2 − b<sup>2</sup> + (c − 2)/2 = 3 − b<sup>2</sup>; dividing by 1/2 gives 2 so b<sup>2</sup> = 2.
a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7.

qs.stem: The number of elements in the relation R = {(x, y) : 4x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> < 52, x, y ∈ Z} is :
steps: Count integer y for each integer x with y<sup>2</sup> < 52 − 4x<sup>2</sup>.
x = 0: |y| ≤ 7, 15 values. x = ±1: |y| ≤ 6, 13 each. x = ±2: |y| ≤ 5, 11 each. x = ±3: |y| ≤ 3, 7 each. |x| ≥ 4 impossible.

qs.stem: Let S = {z ∈ C : 4z<sup>2</sup> + z̄ = 0}. Then ∑<sub>z∈S</sub> |z|<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: Taking moduli: 4|z|<sup>2</sup> = |z|, so z = 0 or |z| = 1/4.
For |z| = 1/4, z z̄ = 1/16 and z̄ = −4z<sup>2</sup> give −4z<sup>3</sup> = 1/16, z<sup>3</sup> = −1/64: three roots, all with |z|<sup>2</sup> = 1/16.

qs.stem: Let a = 2i − j + k and b = λj + 2k, λ ∈ Z be two vectors. Let c = a × b and d be a vector of magnitude 2 in yz-plane. If |c| = √53, then the maximum possible value of (c · d)2 is equal to :
steps: c = a × b = (−(2 + λ), −4, 2λ); |c|2 = 5λ2 + 4λ + 20 = 53 gives λ = −3 (integer), so c = (1, −4, −6).
d = (0, 2cosθ, 2sinθ): c·d = −8cosθ − 12 sinθ.
Max of the square = 8<sup>2</sup> + 12<sup>2</sup> = 208.

qs.stem: Let L be the line (x + 1)/2 = (y + 1)/3 = (z + 3)/6 and let S be the set of all points (a, b, c) on L, whose distance from the line (x + 1)/2 = (y + 1)/3 = (z − 9)/0 along the line L is 7. Then ∑<sub>(a,b,c)∈S</sub> (a + b + c) is equal to :
steps: L meets the plane z = 9 where −3 + 6λ = 9, λ = 2: Q = (3, 5, 9), which lies on the second line.
Points of L at distance 7 from Q: Q ± 7·(2, 3, 6)/7 = (5, 8, 15) and (1, 2, 3).
Sum of coordinates: 28 + 6 = 34.

qs.stem: If the mean deviation about the median of the numbers k, 2k, 3k, ......, 1000k is 500, then k<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: Median = 500.5k, and deviations are |i − 500.5||k| for i = 1..1000.
Mean deviation = 250|k| = 500, so |k| = 2 and k<sup>2</sup> = 4.

qs.stem: The area of the region A = {(x, y) : 4x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> ≤ 8 and y<sup>2</sup> ≤ 4x} is :
steps: Curves meet where 4x<sup>2</sup> + 4x = 8, x = 1 (y = ±2); the ellipse reaches x = √2.
Area = 2[∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> 2√x dx + ∫<sub>1</sub><sup>√2</sup> 2√(2 − x<sup>2</sup>) dx] = 2[4/3 + 2(π/4 − 1/2)].

qs.stem: Let a vector a = √2 i − j + λk, λ > 0, make an obtuse angle with the vector b = −λ2i + 4√2 j + 4√2 k and an angle θ, π/6 < θ < π/2, with the positive z-axis. If the set of all possible values of λ is (α, β) − {γ}, then α + β + γ is equal to ______.
steps: a·b < 0: −√2λ2 − 4√2 + 4√2λ < 0, i.e. (λ − 2)2 > 0, so λ ≠ 2.
cosθ = λ/√(3 + λ<sup>2</sup>) lies in (0, √3/2): 4λ<sup>2</sup> < 3(3 + λ<sup>2</sup>), λ < 3.
λ ∈ (0, 3) − {2}, so α + β + γ = 0 + 3 + 2 = 5.

qs.stem: Let S be the set of the first 11 natural numbers. Then the number of elements in A = {B ⊆ S : n(B) ≥ 2 and the product of all elements of B is even} is ______.
steps: Subsets with at least 2 elements: 2<sup>11</sup> − 1 − 11 = 2036.
Subsets with an odd product use only the 6 odd numbers: 2<sup>6</sup> − 1 − 6 = 57 (size ≥ 2).
Required = 2036 − 57 = 1979.

qs.stem: Suppose a, b, c are in A.P. and a<sup>2</sup>, 2b<sup>2</sup>, c<sup>2</sup> are in G.P. If a < b < c and a + b + c = 1, then 9(a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup>) is equal to ______.
steps: b = 1/3, a = 1/3 − d, c = 1/3 + d. G.P.: 4b<sup>4</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>c<sup>2</sup>, so ac = ±2b<sup>2</sup> = ±2/9.
ac = 1/9 − d<sup>2</sup>; +2/9 gives d<sup>2</sup> < 0, so ac = −2/9 and d<sup>2</sup> = 1/3.
a<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> = 2/9 + 2d<sup>2</sup> = 8/9, so a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> = 1 and 9(·) = 9.

qs.stem: Let [.] be the greatest integer function. If α = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>64</sup> (x<sup>1/3</sup> − [x<sup>1/3</sup>]) dx, then (1/π) ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>απ</sup> (sin<sup>2</sup>θ / (sin<sup>6</sup>θ + cos<sup>6</sup>θ)) dθ is equal to ______.
steps: ∫x<sup>1/3</sup> = (3/4)(64)<sup>4/3</sup> = 192; ∫[x<sup>1/3</sup>] = 1·7 + 2·19 + 3·37 = 156; α = 36.

The integrand has period π, so the integral is 36 ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π</sup>. Using sin<sup>6</sup> + cos<sup>6</sup> = 1 − (3/4)sin<sup>2</sup>2θ and the sin↔cos symmetry, ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π</sup> = (1/2)∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π</sup> dθ/(1 − (3/4)sin<sup>2</sup>2θ).
∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π</sup> dφ/(1 − k sin<sup>2</sup>φ) = π/√(1 − k) = 2π, so ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π</sup> = π and the answer is (36)(π)/π = 36.

qs.stem: Let cos(α + β) = −1/10 and sin(α − β) = 3/8, where 0 < α < π/3 and 0 < β < π/4. If tan 2α = 3(1 − r√5)/(√11(s + √5)), r, s ∈ N, then r + s is equal to ______.
steps: α + β lies in (π/2, 7π/12), so tan(α + β) = −√99 = −3√11. α − β lies in (0, π/3): tan(α − β) = 3/√55.
tan 2α = (T<sub>1</sub> + T<sub>2</sub>)/(1 − T<sub>1</sub>T<sub>2</sub>) with T<sub>1</sub>T<sub>2</sub> = −9/√5: numerator (3 − 33√5)/√55, denominator (√5 + 9)/√5.
tan 2α = 3(1 − 11√5)/(√11(9 + √5)), so r = 11, s = 9, r + s = 20.

qs.stem: In parallax method for the determination of focal length of a concave mirror, the object should always be placed :
steps: The parallax method locates a real image by making it coincide (no parallax) with an image needle, so a real image must form.
A concave mirror forms a real image for any object beyond the focus (u > f).
Between P and F the image is virtual, so that region cannot be used; both regions F-C and beyond C work, hence any point beyond F.
opts: between the focus (F) and the centre of curvature (C) of the mirror ONLY
beyond the centre of the curvature (C) of the mirror ONLY
at any point beyond the focus (F) of the mirror
between the pole (P) and the focus (F) of the concave mirror ONLY

qs.stem: If ε, E and t represent the free space permittivity, electric field and time respectively, then the unit of (εE)/(t) will be :
steps: εE has the dimensions of electric displacement, i.e. charge per unit area: C/m<sup>2</sup> (from Gauss law, εE · area = charge).
Dividing by time: (C/s)/m<sup>2</sup> = A/m<sup>2</sup>.

qs.stem: Figure shows the circuit that contains three resistances (9Ω each) and two inductors ( 4 mH each). The reading of ammeter at the moment switch K is turned ON, is ________ A.
steps: At the instant the switch is closed, an inductor opposes any change in current, so each inductor branch carries zero current and acts like an open circuit.
Only the middle 9 Ω resistor then conducts, so R<sub>eff</sub> = 9 Ω.
Ammeter reading = V/R = 9/9 = 1 A.

qs.stem: The smallest wavelength of Lyman series is 91 nm. The difference between the largest wavelengths of Paschen and Balmer series is nearly__________ nm .
steps: Lyman limit: 1/λ = R, so R = 1/91 nm<sup>-1</sup>.
Largest Balmer wavelength (3→2): 1/λ = R(1/4 − 1/9) = 5R/36, so λ = 36/(5R) = 36×91/5 = 655.2 nm.
Largest Paschen wavelength (4→3): 1/λ = R(1/9 − 1/16) = 7R/144, so λ = 144×91/7 = 1872 nm.
Difference = 1872 − 655.2 ≈ 1217 nm.

qs.stem: Five positive charges each having charge q are placed at the vertices of a pentagon as shown in the figure. The electric potential (V) and the electric field (E) at the center O of the pentagon due to these five positive charges are :
steps: Potential is a scalar: each charge is at distance r, so V = 5 × q/(4πε<sub>o</sub>r) = 5q/(4πε<sub>o</sub>r).
The five equal charges sit symmetrically on a regular pentagon, so their field vectors at the centre (equal magnitudes, directions 72° apart) sum to zero: E = 0.

qs.stem:
The correct truth table for the given input data of the following logic gate is :
(Inputs A, B feed an AND gate whose output goes through a NOT gate; inputs C, D feed an OR gate; the NOT output and the OR output feed a second AND gate, whose output goes through a NOT gate to give Y.)
steps: Write the output: Y = NOT[ NOT(A·B) · (C + D) ] = A·B + NOT(C + D).
(1,1,0,1): A·B = 1, so Y = 1. (0,0,1,1): A·B = 0 and C + D = 1, so Y = 0.
(1,0,1,0): A·B = 0 and C + D = 1, so Y = 0. (1,1,1,1): A·B = 1, so Y = 1.
The rows 1, 0, 0, 1 match option (4).

qs.stem: A laser beam has intensity of 4.0×10<sup>14</sup> W/m<sup>2</sup>. The amplitude of magnetic field associated with beam is ___________ T. (Take ε<sub>o</sub> = 8.85×10<sup>−12</sup> C<sup>2</sup>/Nm<sup>2</sup> and c = 3×10<sup>8</sup> m/s)
steps: Intensity I = (1/2) ε<sub>o</sub> c E<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> with E<sub>0</sub> = cB<sub>0</sub>, so I = (1/2) ε<sub>o</sub> c<sup>3</sup> B<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>.
B<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> = 2I/(ε<sub>o</sub>c<sup>3</sup>) = (8×10<sup>14</sup>)/(8.85×10<sup>−12</sup> × 2.7×10<sup>25</sup>) ≈ 3.35.
B<sub>0</sub> ≈ 1.83 T.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A satellite is moving around earth in the orbit very close to the earth surface. The time period of revolution of satellite depends upon the density of earth.
Statement II : The time period of revolution of the satellite is T = 2π√(Re/g) (for satellite very close to the earth surface), where Re radius of earth and g acceleration due to gravity.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: For a near-surface orbit, GM/R<sub>e</sub><sup>2</sup> = g = v<sup>2</sup>/R<sub>e</sub>, giving T = 2πR<sub>e</sub>/v = 2π√(R<sub>e</sub>/g): Statement II is true.
Substituting g = (4/3)πGρR<sub>e</sub> gives T = 2π√(3/(4πGρ)), which depends on the density ρ: Statement I is true.
Both are true.
opts: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

qs.stem: The wavelength of light, while it is passing through water is 540 nm. The refractive index of water is 4/3. The wavelength of the same light when it is passing through a transparent medium having refractive index of 3/2 is __________ nm.
steps: Frequency is fixed, so λ ∝ 1/n, i.e. n<sub>1</sub>λ<sub>1</sub> = n<sub>2</sub>λ<sub>2</sub> (both equal λ in vacuum × n/n).
λ<sub>2</sub> = 480 nm.

qs.stem: Three small identical bubbles of water having same charge on each coalesce to form a bigger bubble. Then the ratio of the potentials on one initial bubble and that on the resultant bigger bubble is :
steps: Volume conserved: 3r<sup>3</sup> = R<sup>3</sup>, so R = 3<sup>1/3</sup> r. Charge adds: Q = 3q.
V<sub>small</sub> = kq/r and V<sub>big</sub> = k(3q)/(3<sup>1/3</sup> r) = 3<sup>2/3</sup> kq/r.
Ratio V<sub>small</sub> : V<sub>big</sub> = 1 : 3<sup>2/3</sup>.

qs.stem:
In an open organ pipe v3 and v6 are 3rd and 6th harmonic frequencies, respectively. If v6 − v3 = 2200 Hz then length of the pipe is __________ mm.
(Take velocity of sound in air is 330 m/s)
steps: For an open pipe the n-th harmonic is n v/(2L), so v<sub>6</sub> − v<sub>3</sub> = 3v/(2L).

qs.stem: Light is incident on a metallic plate having work function 110×10<sup>−20</sup> J. If the produced photoelectrons have zero kinetic energy then the angular frequency of the incident light is __________ rad/s. (h = 6.63×10<sup>−34</sup> J.s).
steps: Zero kinetic energy means incident photon energy equals the work function (threshold): hν = φ.
ν = 110×10<sup>−20</sup>/6.63×10<sup>−34</sup> ≈ 1.66×10<sup>15</sup> Hz.
ω = 2πν ≈ 6.283 × 1.66×10<sup>15</sup> ≈ 1.04×10<sup>16</sup> rad/s.

qs.stem: An electric power line having total resistance of 2Ω, delivers 1 kW of power at 250 V . The percentage efficiency of transmission line is __________ .
steps: Current in the line I = P/V = 1000/250 = 4 A.
Power lost in the line = I<sup>2</sup>R = 16 × 2 = 32 W, so input power = 1000 + 32 = 1032 W.
Efficiency = 1000/1032 × 100 ≈ 96.9 %.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: For a mechanical system of many particles total kinetic energy is the sum of kinetic energies of all the particles.
Statement II: The total kinetic energy can be the sum of kinetic energy of the center of mass w.r.t to the origin and the kinetic energy of all the particles w.r.t. the center of mass as the reference.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Kinetic energy is a scalar, so the total is simply the sum of the energies of the individual particles: Statement I is true.
By Konig theorem, K = (1/2)M v<sub>cm</sub><sup>2</sup> + Σ(1/2)m<sub>i</sub>v<sub>i,cm</sub><sup>2</sup> (the cross term vanishes): Statement II is true.
opts: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

qs.stem: When a part of a straight capillary tube is placed vertically in a liquid, the liquid raises upto certain height h. If the inner radius of the capillary tube, density of the liquid and surface tension of the liquid decrease by 1% each, then the height of the liquid in the tube will change by _________%.
steps: Capillary rise h = 2T cosθ/(ρ g r), so for small changes Δh/h = ΔT/T − Δρ/ρ − Δr/r.
With each of T, ρ, r falling by 1 %: Δh/h = (−1) − (−1) − (−1) = +1 %.

qs.stem: A uniform bar of length 12 cm and mass 20 m lies on a smooth horizontal table. Two point masses m and 2m are moving in opposite directions with same speed of v and in the same plane as the bar, as shown in figure. These masses strike the bar simultaneously and get stuck to it. After collision the entire system is rotating with angular frequency ω. The ratio of v and ω is :
steps: The 2m mass hits 2 cm on one side of the bar centre and m hits 4 cm on the other side, moving in opposite directions, so their angular momenta about the centre add. The combined centre of mass stays at the bar centre (m×4 − 2m×2 = 0).
L = m v (4) + 2m v (2) = 8 m v (lengths in cm).
ω = L/I = 8v/264, so v/ω = 33 (with v in cm/s).
qs.fig: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' stroke='currentColor' fill='none' stroke-width='1.5' font-size='11'><rect x='20' y='60' width='240' height='24'/><path d='M100 20V58M96 50L100 58L104 50'/><text x='94' y='15' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'>2m</text><path d='M220 125V86M216 94L220 86L224 94'/><text x='216' y='140' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'>m</text><path d='M20 100H260M20 96V104M260 96V104' stroke-width='1'/><text x='125' y='112' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'>12 cm</text><path d='M100 48H140M140 48V60M140 48H220' stroke-dasharray='3 3' stroke-width='1'/><text x='112' y='44' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'>2 cm</text><text x='170' y='44' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'>4 cm</text></svg>

qs.stem: An insulated cylinder of volume 60 cm<sup>3</sup> is filled with a gas at 27<sup>o</sup>C and 2 atmospheric pressure. Then the gas is compressed making the final volume as 20 cm<sup>3</sup> while allowing the temperature to rise to 77<sup>o</sup>C. The final pressure is ________ atmospheric pressure.
steps: Same amount of gas: P<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub>/T<sub>1</sub> = P<sub>2</sub>V<sub>2</sub>/T<sub>2</sub> with T in kelvin (300 K and 350 K).

qs.stem:
Two masses m and 2 m are connected by a light string going over a pulley (disc) of mass 30 m with radius r = 0.1 m. The pulley is mounted in a vertical plane and it is free to rotate about its axis. The 2 m mass is released from rest and its speed when it has descended through a height of 3.6 m is – (m/s)
(Assume string does not slip and g = 10 m/s2)
steps: Energy: net loss of potential energy = 2mgh − mgh = mgh = 36m (h = 3.6 m, g = 10).
Kinetic energy gained = (1/2)(2m)v<sup>2</sup> + (1/2)m v<sup>2</sup> + (1/2)(1/2)(30m)r<sup>2</sup>(v/r)<sup>2</sup> = (1 + 0.5 + 7.5) m v<sup>2</sup> = 9 m v<sup>2</sup>.
36 m = 9 m v<sup>2</sup>, so v = 2 m/s.

qs.stem: A capacitor P with capacitance 10 × 10<sup>−6</sup> F is fully charged with a potential difference of 6.0 V and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor P is connected across another capacitor Q with capacitance 20 × 10<sup>−6</sup> F. The charge on capacitor Q when equilibrium is established will be α × 10<sup>−5</sup> C (assume capacitor Q does not have any charge initially), the value of α is _______.
steps: Initial charge on P: 10µF × 6 V = 60 µC, which is conserved.
In parallel both reach the same voltage V = 60/(10 + 20) = 2 V.
Q<sub>Q</sub> = 20 µF × 2 V = 40 µC = 4 × 10<sup>−5</sup> C, so α = 4.

qs.stem: A conducting circular loop is rotated about its diameter at a constant angular speed of 100 rad/s in a magnetic field of 0.5 T perpendicular to the axis of rotation. When the loop is rotated by 30<sup>o</sup> from the horizontal position, the induced EMF is 15.4 mV . The radius of the loop is ________ mm. (Take π = 22/7)
steps: Flux Φ = BπR<sup>2</sup> cosωt, so emf = BπR<sup>2</sup>ω sinωt.
At ωt = 30°: 15.4×10<sup>−3</sup> = 0.5 × (22/7) × R<sup>2</sup> × 100 × 0.5 = 78.57 R<sup>2</sup>.
R<sup>2</sup> = 1.96×10<sup>−4</sup> m<sup>2</sup>, so R = 0.014 m = 14 mm.

qs.stem: A cylindrical conductor of length 2 m and area of cross-section 0.2 mm<sup>2</sup> carries an electric current of 1.6 A when its ends are connected to a 2 V battery. Mobility of electrons in the conductor is α × 10<sup>−3</sup> m<sup>2</sup> / V.s . The value of α is : (electron concentration = 5×10<sup>28</sup> / m<sup>3</sup> and electron charge = 1.6×10<sup>−19</sup> C)
steps: Drift speed v<sub>d</sub> = I/(neA) and field E = V/L, so mobility μ = v<sub>d</sub>/E = IL/(neAV).
μ = (1.6 × 2)/(5×10<sup>28</sup> × 1.6×10<sup>−19</sup> × 0.2×10<sup>−6</sup> × 2) = 3.2/(3.2×10<sup>3</sup>) = 10<sup>−3</sup> m<sup>2</sup>/V.s.
Hence α = 1.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Elements 'X' and 'Y' are the most and least electronegative elements, respectively among N, As, Sb and P. The nature of the oxides X2O3 and Y2O3 is acidic and amphoteric, respectively.
Statement II: BCl3 is covalent in nature and gets hydrolysed in water. It produces [B(OH)4]− and [B(H2O)6]3+ in aqueous medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Electronegativity falls down group 15, so X = N (most) and Y = Sb (least).
N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> is acidic and Sb<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> is amphoteric, so Statement I is true.
BCl<sub>3</sub> hydrolyses to B(OH)<sub>3</sub> + 3HCl; it does not give [B(OH)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>−</sup> and [B(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3+</sup>, so Statement II is false.
Statement I true, Statement II false: option (4).
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

qs.stem: At T(K), 100 g of 98% H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (w/w) aqueous solution is mixed with 100 g of 49% H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (w/w) aqueous solution. What is the mole fraction of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> in the resultant solution? (Given: Atomic mass H = 1u; S = 32u; O = 16u). (Assume that temperature after mixing remains constant)
steps: Mass of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> = 98 + 49 = 147 g, so moles = 147/98 = 1.5.
Total mass = 200 g, so water = 53 g = 53/18 ≈ 2.94 mol.

qs.stem: Which of the following mixture gives a buffer solution with pH = 9.25? Given: pK<sub>b</sub>(NH<sub>4</sub>OH) = 4.75
steps: pH = 9.25 means pOH = 4.75 = pK<sub>b</sub>, so [salt] = [base] is needed.
Option 1: base 100 mmol, HCl 50 mmol, giving 50 mmol NH<sub>4</sub>Cl and 50 mmol NH<sub>4</sub>OH left: ratio 1, a buffer.
Option 2: acid (100 mmol) exceeds base (80 mmol); option 3: equal amounts (100 mmol each) give only salt; option 4: 300 mmol base and 100 mmol salt, ratio not 1.
Hence option (1).
opts: 0.2 M NH<sub>4</sub>OH (0.5 L) + 0.1 M HCl (0.5 L)
0.2 M NH<sub>4</sub>OH (0.4 L) + 0.1 M HCl (1 L)
0.5 M NH<sub>4</sub>OH (0.2 L) + 0.2 M HCl (0.5 L)
0.4 M NH<sub>4</sub>OH (1 L) + 0.1 M HCl (1 L)

qs.stem:
[Ni(PPh3)2Cl2] is a paramagnetic complex. Identify the INCORRECT statements about this complex.
A. The complex exhibits geometrical isomerism.
B. The complex is white in colour.
C. The calculated spin-only magnetic moment of the complex is 2.84 BM.
D. The calculated CFSE (Crystal Field Stabilization Energy) of Ni in this complex is −0.8Δo.
E. The geometrical arrangement of ligands in this complex is similar to that in Ni(CO)4.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Ni<sup>2+</sup> is d<sup>8</sup>; being paramagnetic with Cl<sup>−</sup> and PPh<sub>3</sub>, the complex is tetrahedral (like Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub>), so E is correct.
Tetrahedral complexes show no geometrical isomerism, so A is incorrect; it has 2 unpaired electrons, so it is coloured (not white), so B is incorrect.
μ = √(2×4) = 2.83 BM ≈ 2.84, so C is correct.
CFSE (e<sup>4</sup>t<sub>2</sub><sup>4</sup>) = −0.6×4 + 0.4×4 = −0.8Δ<sub>t</sub>, not Δ<sub>o</sub>, so D is incorrect. Incorrect: A, B, D.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: C < O < N < F is the correct order in terms of first ionization enthalpy values.
Statement II: S > Se > Te > Po > O is the correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy values.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Statement I: across period 2 ionization enthalpy rises with Z<sub>eff</sub>, with the usual N > O anomaly (half-filled 2p<sup>3</sup>), giving C < O < N < F: true.
Statement II: group 16 electron gain enthalpy magnitude: S (−200) > Se (−195) > Te (−190) > Po (−174) > O (−141) kJ/mol: true.
Both true: option (1).
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

qs.stem: The compound A, C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub> reacts with acetophenone to form a single product via cross-Aldol condensation. The compound A on reaction with conc. NaOH forms a substituted benzyl alcohol as one of the two products. The compound A is:
steps: Giving a benzyl alcohol plus another product with conc. NaOH is a Cannizzaro reaction, so A is an aldehyde with no α-hydrogen.
Such an aldehyde also gives a single crossed-aldol (Claisen-Schmidt) product with acetophenone, since it cannot enolise itself.
C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub> matches 4-CH<sub>3</sub>O–C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>4</sub>–CHO (4-hydroxybenzaldehyde would be C<sub>7</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O<sub>2</sub>), so A is option (1).

qs.stem: The energy of first (lowest) Balmer line of H atom is x J. The energy (in J) of second Balmer line of H atom is:
steps: First Balmer line: 3 → 2, energy ∝ (1/4 − 1/9) = 5/36.
Second Balmer line: 4 → 2, energy ∝ (1/4 − 1/16) = 3/16.

qs.stem: Among H<sub>2</sub>S, H<sub>2</sub>O, NF<sub>3</sub>, NH<sub>3</sub> and CHCl<sub>3</sub>, identify the molecule (X) with lowest dipole moment value. The number of lone pairs of electrons present on the central atom of the molecule (X) is:
steps: Approximate dipole moments (D): H<sub>2</sub>S 0.95, H<sub>2</sub>O 1.85, NF<sub>3</sub> 0.23, NH<sub>3</sub> 1.47, CHCl<sub>3</sub> 1.04.
In NF<sub>3</sub> the N–F bond dipoles oppose the dipole of the lone pair, so the net value is the lowest.
The central N in NF<sub>3</sub> carries 1 lone pair.

qs.stem:
Identify the correct statements:
A. Hydrated salts can be used as primary standard.
B. Primary standard should not undergo any reaction with air.
C. Reactions of primary standard with another substance should be instantaneous and stoichiometric.
D. Primary standard should not be soluble in water.
E. Primary standard should have low relative molar mass.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: A is true: stable hydrates of fixed composition (e.g. Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>·10H<sub>2</sub>O as quoted in the booklet's example) can serve.
B and C are true: a standard must be unreactive to air and react fast and with known stoichiometry.
D is false (it must dissolve to make a standard solution); E is false (a high molar mass reduces weighing error). So A, B, C.
opts: A, B, C and E Only

qs.stem:
Correct statements regarding Arrhenius equation among the following are:
A. Factor e−Ea/RT corresponds to fraction of molecules having kinetic energy less than Ea.
B. At a given temperature, lower the Ea, faster is the reaction.
C. Increase in temperature by about 10°C doubles the rate of reaction.
D. Plot of log k vs 1/T gives a straight line with slope = −Ea/R.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: A is false: e<sup>−Ea/RT</sup> is the fraction of molecules with energy equal to or greater than E<sub>a</sub>.
B is true: a lower barrier lets more molecules react, so k is larger. C is true as the usual rule of thumb (temperature coefficient about 2).
D is false: the slope of log k vs 1/T is −E<sub>a</sub>/(2.303R), not −E<sub>a</sub>/R. So B and C.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The first ionization enthalpy of Cr is lower than that of Mn.
Statement II: The second and third ionization enthalpies of Cr are higher than those of Mn.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: IE<sub>1</sub>: Cr (3d<sup>5</sup>4s<sup>1</sup>) is lower than Mn (3d<sup>5</sup>4s<sup>2</sup>), so Statement I is true.

IE<sub>2</sub>: Cr<sup>+</sup> is the stable d<sup>5</sup> ion, so IE<sub>2</sub>(Cr) > IE<sub>2</sub>(Mn); but IE<sub>3</sub>: Mn<sup>2+</sup> is d<sup>5</sup>, so IE<sub>3</sub>(Mn) > IE<sub>3</sub>(Cr).
The third ionization enthalpy of Cr is not higher, so Statement II is false: option (4).
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

qs.stem:
List-I (Reaction of Glucose with) / List-II (Product formed):
A. Hydroxylamine / I. Gluconic acid
B. Br2 water / II. Glucose pentacetate
C. Excess acetic anhydride / III. Saccharic acid
D. Concentrated HNO3 / IV. Glucoxime
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Glucose + NH<sub>2</sub>OH gives the oxime, glucoxime: A-IV.
Mild oxidant Br<sub>2</sub>/H<sub>2</sub>O oxidises only the CHO to COOH, giving gluconic acid: B-I.
Excess acetic anhydride acetylates all five OH groups, giving glucose pentaacetate: C-II.
Conc. HNO<sub>3</sub> oxidises both ends to the dicarboxylic saccharic acid: D-III. This is option (4).

qs.stem:
A + 2B → AB2
36.0 g of 'A' (Molar mass: 60 g mol−1) and 56.0 g of 'B' (Molar mass: 80 g mol−1) are allowed to react. Which of the following statements are correct?
A. 'A' is the limiting reagent.
B. 77.0 g of AB2 is formed.
C. Molar mass of AB2 is 140 g mol−1.
D. 15.0 g of A is left unreacted after the completion of reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Moles: A = 36/60 = 0.6; B = 56/80 = 0.7. B needs 2 per A, so B (0.7/2 = 0.35) is limiting; A is not.
AB<sub>2</sub> formed = 0.35 mol; molar mass = 60 + 2×80 = 220 g/mol, so mass = 0.35×220 = 77 g (B true, C false).
A left = 0.6 − 0.35 = 0.25 mol = 15 g (D true). So B and D.

qs.stem: When 1 g of compound (X) is subjected to Kjeldahl's method for estimation of nitrogen, 15 mL 1 M H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> was neutralized by ammonia evolved. The percentage of nitrogen in compound (X) is:
steps: H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> = 15 mL × 1 M = 15 mmol, which neutralises 2×15 = 30 mmol NH<sub>3</sub>.
Moles of N = 30 mmol, mass = 0.030 × 14 = 0.42 g.

qs.stem:
Consider the following reduction processes:
Al3+ + 3e− → Al(s), E° = −1.66 V
Fe3+ + e− → Fe2+, E° = +0.77 V
Co3+ + e− → Co2+, E° = +1.81 V
Cr3+ + 3e− → Cr(s), E° = −0.74 V
The tendency to act as reducing agent decreases in the:
steps: The reduced species of the couple with the lowest E° is the strongest reducing agent.
Order of E°: Al<sup>3+</sup>/Al (−1.66) < Cr<sup>3+</sup>/Cr (−0.74) < Fe<sup>3+</sup>/Fe<sup>2+</sup> (+0.77) < Co<sup>3+</sup>/Co<sup>2+</sup> (+1.81).
Reducing power: Al > Cr > Fe<sup>2+</sup> > Co<sup>2+</sup>.

qs.stem: Consider A → B (k<sub>1</sub>) and C → D (k<sub>2</sub>) are two reactions. If the rate constant (k<sub>1</sub>) of the A → B reaction can be expressed by log<sub>10</sub> k = 14.34 − (1.5 × 10<sup>4</sup>)/(T/K) and activation energy of C → D reaction (Ea<sub>2</sub>) is 1/5 th of the A → B reaction (Ea<sub>1</sub>), then the value of (Ea<sub>2</sub>) is _____ kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>. (Nearest Integer)
steps: Compare with log k = log A − E<sub>a</sub>/(2.303RT): E<sub>a1</sub>/(2.303R) = 1.5×10<sup>4</sup> K.
E<sub>a1</sub> = 1.5×10<sup>4</sup> × 2.303 × 8.314 ≈ 2.872×10<sup>5</sup> J/mol = 287.2 kJ/mol.
E<sub>a2</sub> = 287.2/5 ≈ 57.4, so 57 kJ/mol.

qs.stem: Consider the following electrochemical cell: Pt|O<sub>2</sub>(g)(1 bar)|HCl(aq)||M<sup>2+</sup>(aq, 1.0 M)|M(s). The pH above which, oxygen gas would start to evolve at anode is _____ (nearest integer). [Given: E°(M<sup>2+</sup>/M) = 0.994 V, E°(O<sub>2</sub>/H<sub>2</sub>O) = 1.23 V standard reduction potential and (RT/F)(2.303) = 0.059 V at the given condition]
steps: Anode (oxidation): H<sub>2</sub>O → 2H<sup>+</sup> + ½O<sub>2</sub> + 2e<sup>−</sup>; the O<sub>2</sub>/H<sub>2</sub>O reduction potential at 1 bar is E = 1.23 − 0.059 pH.
Cathode: M<sup>2+</sup>/M at 1 M, E = 0.994 V.
E<sub>cell</sub> = 0.994 − (1.23 − 0.059 pH) > 0, so 0.059 pH > 0.236 and pH > 4.0, which rounds to 4.

qs.stem: Among the following oxides of 3d elements, the number of mixed oxides are _____. Ti<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, V<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>, Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, Mn<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>, Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>, Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, Co<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>
steps: A mixed oxide has the metal in two oxidation states: Mn<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> = MnO·Mn<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> = FeO·Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, Co<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> = CoO·Co<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>.
Ti<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, V<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>, Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> and Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> have a single oxidation state each, so the count is 3.

qs.stem: The mass of benzanilide obtained from the benzoylation reaction of 5.8 g of aniline, if yield of product is 82%, is _____ g (nearest integer). (Given molar mass in g mol<sup>−1</sup> H: 1, C: 12, N: 14, O: 16)
steps: Aniline C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>NH<sub>2</sub> = 93 g/mol, so moles = 5.8/93 ≈ 0.0624.
Benzanilide C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>NHCOC<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub> = 197 g/mol; theoretical mass = 0.0624 × 197 ≈ 12.3 g.
At 82% yield: 12.3 × 0.82 ≈ 10.1, so 10 g.

qs.stem: If the enthalpy of sublimation of Li is 155 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>, enthalpy of dissociation of F<sub>2</sub> is 150 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>, ionization enthalpy of Li is 520 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>, electron gain enthalpy of F is −313 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>, standard enthalpy of formation of LiF is −594 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>. The magnitude of lattice enthalpy of LiF is _____ kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>. (Nearest Integer)
steps: Born–Haber cycle: Δ<sub>f</sub>H = Δ<sub>sub</sub>H(Li) + IE(Li) + ½Δ<sub>diss</sub>H(F<sub>2</sub>) + Δ<sub>eg</sub>H(F) + Δ<sub>lattice</sub>H.
−594 = 155 + 520 + 75 − 313 + Δ<sub>L</sub>H = 437 + Δ<sub>L</sub>H.
Δ<sub>L</sub>H = −1031 kJ/mol, so the magnitude is 1031.
